transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-09
Start: 10:00am PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM); Lena Cho, Tom Brenner, Aisha O'Neil, Rajiv Malhotra (Horizon Financial)

Summary: Quick weekly security-focused POC sync. Main items: SSO progress, audit logging format and retention, data retention and redaction for embeddings/transcripts, SOC2 evidence timeline.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call then we'll jump into SSO and the logs.
[00:07] Lena Cho: Hi, Lena here. Tom, Aisha, Rajiv also on.
[00:10] Tom Brenner: Yep, Tom on security. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:14] Diego Ramos: Diego from Redwood, I'll take the technical details on logging and RBAC.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Priya from CSM, will track action items.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Cool. First item SSO status — Tom last time you mentioned you had the SAML metadata ready but there was a cert issue?
[00:31] Tom Brenner: Yeah so we tried to post the metadata to the test endpoint, we got a cert mismatch. Looks like our metadata SP entity ID didn't match the assertion consumer URL. We're cleaning that up, should be resolved by end of day tomorrow.
[00:43] Aisha O'Neil: Also question on scoping: do you need full user provisioning or just SSO login for the pilot?
[00:50] Maya Patel: For the pilot we only need SSO login and mapping to a minimal set of RBAC roles. Full SCIM later is fine but not required now.
[00:58] Rajiv Malhotra: Ok that reduces scope. We'll provide a small test group of five users and metadata.
[01:03] Diego Ramos: Great. On our side once we get the metadata we'll configure the IdP and push a test link. There may be a second round if there are mapping mismatches — it's pretty normal.
[01:14] Lena Cho: Next, audit logs. We want to understand what fields you capture and retention options. We need immutable logs for certain events for 90 days.
[01:24] Diego Ramos: Right, our runtime emits per-request audit events. Current fields: timestamp, request_id, user_id (subject), model, route, latency_ms, tokens_in/tokens_out, error code if any, and optionally the request/response hashes. We can include storage location and pipeline id.
[01:41] Tom Brenner: Do you store the raw transcript payloads in logs? We can't keep PII in logs.
[01:47] Diego Ramos: By default we store hashes for request and response; raw transcripts are stored only if customer opts in for debugging. For the pilot we can set redaction and store just metadata and hashes — or keep full payloads in an encrypted bucket if Horizon wants that for debugging.
[02:02] Lena Cho: Ok we need a redaction policy doc. Also, retention periods: can you do a 90-day retention for audit logs and 30-day for conversation transcripts by default?
[02:12] Maya Patel: Yes, those are both supported. We have configurable retention per-type in the Private/ Dedicated configs; hosted has retention options but we can provide a tailored SLA for Horizon in Dedicated.
[02:23] Tom Brenner: For compliance we need attestations around encryption at rest and KMS usage. Where is key management handled?
[02:30] Maya Patel: For hosted we use customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we offer CMEK as an add-on in enterprise. We can provide architecture diagram and the SOC2 section that covers KMS usage.
[02:41] Rajiv Malhotra: And audit logs — are they append-only? Can we stream them to our Splunk?
[02:46] Diego Ramos: Yes, audit log stream is supported via secure forwarder to S3/Kafka/Splunk. We have a delivery connector. We can demo the Splunk pipeline in the next sync.
[02:56] Aisha O'Neil: About SOC 2 — we requested the report and any user access lists and system architecture. Timeline?
[03:03] Maya Patel: We can send the SOC 2 Type II report and the security questionnaire by Friday 2025-12-12. We'll include an architecture diagram and our control mappings.
[03:12] Tom Brenner: Will that include evidence for change management and access control?
[03:16] Maya Patel: High-level yes, and we can pull specific evidence examples under NDA. For the pilot we'll provide the artifacts needed for your security review.
[03:24] Lena Cho: Great. Also want to confirm log retention is queryable — i.e., we can export and search logs for the 90-day window?
[03:30] Diego Ramos: Yep. Export and SIEM integration supported. Logs are in JSONL format and indexed for quick search, or shipped to your SIEM.
[03:38] Lena Cho: Perfect. Next, data retention for embeddings and transcripts: do you retain embeddings by default? How long?
[03:44] Diego Ramos: By default, embeddings generated during the session are ephemeral unless you opt into storage for retrieval/semantic search. For the pilot we can configure a 30-day retention and then auto-delete. We also support immediate purge APIs for customer-initiated deletes.
[03:58] Aisha O'Neil: If we enable storage for embeddings, are they encrypted with our KMS?
[04:02] Maya Patel: Yes, stored embeddings in Dedicated/Private are encrypted with CMEK; hosted can be configured with CMEK as part of enterprise package.
[04:09] Tom Brenner: Do you have support for field-level redaction or PIi detection pre-ingest?
[04:14] Diego Ramos: We have a pre-ingest redaction pipeline that can be enabled; it can do regex-based removal and ML PII detection to redact or mask fields before indexing. We'll share the pipeline config as a sample.
[04:26] Rajiv Malhotra: Good. For the pilot audit we need to capture who accessed model outputs and when — are access events logged at token-level or per-request?
[04:35] Diego Ramos: Per-request granularity with request-level metadata. For deeper traces we can include KV cache access logs but that is heavier. For compliance the per-request audit logs should suffice.
[04:46] Priya Singh: Quick question from the last POC report — we saw higher tail latency on longer sequences. Has that been addressed?
[04:51] Diego Ramos: Yes, we made batching and KV cache adjustments for Horizon traffic profile; current tail latency is improved — we'll run a 24-hour benchmark and share results.
[04:58] Lena Cho: Ok, that helps. One more: who will be the contact for incident response? We need an IR contact and escalation matrix.
[05:06] Maya Patel: Maya will be the primary AE contact, Diego and our on-call infra team are the technical escalation. We'll share an incident response runbook and SLA matrix.
[05:15] Tom Brenner: We also request proof of periodic penetration testing and third-party audits.
[05:20] Maya Patel: We can share summary of penetration test outcomes and vendor names; detailed reports require an NDA.
[05:26] Lena Cho: Sounds good. Any blockers from Horizon side?
[05:30] Tom Brenner: SSO metadata fix in progress. Once that's up we'll do the SSO test. Also will need the audit log sample to validate retention and schema.
[05:39] Maya Patel: Action items recap: we'll send SOC2 report, security deck, architecture diagram; Diego will send sample logs; Tom will share SAML metadata and test users; Priya will schedule the RBAC demo.
[05:51] Priya Singh: I'll send a calendar invite for next week for RBAC and the Splunk pipeline demo.
[05:57] Maya Patel: Anything else?
[05:58] Rajiv Malhotra: No, thanks.
[05:59] Lena Cho: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

Close: 10:46am PST
